hook.text: The genome is the blueprint, the transcriptome the message, the proteome the worker — multi-omics reads all three.

buildup.text: Genomics finds mutations, transcriptomics measures expression, proteomics identifies proteins — each tells part of the story.

discovery.text: Metabolomics measures small molecules — the actual output of cellular activity, closest to the patient's phenotype.

twist.text: Integrating omics layers requires massive computational power — terabytes of data per patient, analyzed by AI.

climax.text: Multi-omics signatures predict drug response better than any single data type — the whole exceeds the sum of parts.

punchline.text: Genome, transcriptome, proteome, metabolome — read them all, understand the patient.

quiz.question: Why is multi-omics better than genomics alone for predicting drug response?
options: Genomics cannot detect any disease-related mutations
Integrating multiple data layers captures gene activity, protein levels, and metabolism, giving a fuller biological picture
Multi-omics is cheaper and faster than genomic sequencing

details.summary: Multi-omics integration combines data from genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, and epigenomics to create comprehensive biological profiles of patients. This holistic view reveals disease mechanisms and treatment responses that any single omics layer cannot capture alone.
details.whyItMatters: Genes are just blueprints. Understanding disease requires knowing what is actually expressed, what proteins are made, what metabolites are produced, and how regulation changes.
takeaways: No single omics layer explains disease biology completely on its own
Integration reveals causal pathways from genetic variants to clinical outcomes
AI and machine learning are essential for interpreting multi-dimensional data

faq.question: Why is genomic data alone insufficient for personalized medicine?
faq.answer: A genetic variant may not affect protein levels due to regulatory compensation. Gene expression varies by tissue and time. Post-translational protein modifications alter function unpredictably. The microbiome and environment modulate genetic effects. Multi-omics captures these additional layers.

faq.question: How is multi-omics data integrated computationally?
faq.answer: Machine learning models like autoencoders and graph neural networks find patterns across omics layers simultaneously. Network analysis links genetic variants to expression changes to protein alterations to metabolic effects.
